title_en: Regulations on the Supervision and Administration of Medical Devices

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated to ensure the safety and effectiveness of medical devices, safeguard human health and life safety, and promote the development of the medical device industry.

Article 2 These Regulations shall apply to the research, development, production, operation, and use of medical devices, as well as the supervision and administration thereof, within the territory of the People's Republic of China.

Article 3 The drug regulatory department of the State Council shall be responsible for the supervision and administration of medical devices nationwide.
The relevant departments of the State Council shall, within their respective functions and duties, be responsible for the supervision and administration of matters related to medical devices.

Article 4 The local people's governments at or above the county level shall strengthen their leadership over the supervision and administration of medical devices within their respective administrative regions, organize and coordinate the supervision and administration of medical devices and the response to emergencies within their respective administrative regions, strengthen the capacity building for the supervision and administration of medical devices, and provide guarantees for the safety of medical devices.
The departments responsible for drug regulation of the local people's governments at or above the county level shall be responsible for the supervision and administration of medical devices within their respective administrative regions. The relevant departments of the local people's governments at or above the county level shall, within their respective functions and duties, be responsible for the supervision and administration of matters related to medical devices.
Article 5 The supervision and administration of medical devices shall follow the principles of risk management, whole-process control, science-based regulation, and social co-governance.

Article 6 The State shall implement classified management of medical devices according to the degree of risk.
Class I refers to medical devices with a low degree of risk, for which routine management may ensure their safety and effectiveness.
Class II refers to medical devices with a moderate degree of risk, which require strict control and management to ensure their safety and effectiveness.
Class III refers to medical devices with a relatively high degree of risk, which require special measures and strict control and management to ensure their safety and effectiveness.
In evaluating the degree of risk of a medical device, factors such as the intended purpose, structural characteristics, and method of use of the medical device shall be considered.
The drug regulatory department of the State Council shall be responsible for formulating the classification rules and classification catalog for medical devices, and shall, based on the production, operation, and use of medical devices, promptly analyze and evaluate changes in the risk of medical devices and adjust the classification rules and classification catalog. In formulating and adjusting the classification rules and classification catalog, the opinions of medical device registrants, filing persons, production and operation enterprises, user units, and industry organizations shall be fully heard, and international medical device classification practices shall be referenced. The classification rules and classification catalog for medical devices shall be published to the public.

Article 7 Medical device products shall comply with the mandatory national standards for medical devices; where there are no mandatory national standards, they shall comply with the mandatory industry standards for medical devices.

Article 8 The State shall formulate plans and policies for the medical device industry, incorporate medical device innovation into development priorities, grant priority review and approval to innovative medical devices, support the clinical promotion and use of innovative medical devices, and promote the high-quality development of the medical device industry. The drug regulatory department of the State Council shall cooperate with the relevant departments of the State Council to implement the national medical device industry plans and guiding policies.

Article 9 The State shall improve the medical device innovation system, support basic research and applied research on medical devices, promote the dissemination and application of new medical device technologies, and provide support in areas such as science and technology project establishment, financing, credit, bidding and procurement, and medical insurance. The State shall support enterprises in establishing or jointly establishing research and development institutions, encourage enterprises to cooperate with higher education institutions, research institutes, medical institutions, and others in conducting research and innovation on medical devices, strengthen the protection of intellectual property rights in medical devices, and enhance the independent innovation capability in medical devices.

Article 10 The State shall strengthen the informatization development of the supervision and administration of medical devices, improve the level of online government services, and facilitate the administrative licensing and filing of medical devices.

Article 11 Medical device industry organizations shall strengthen industry self-discipline, promote the construction of a credit system, urge enterprises to carry out production and operation activities in accordance with law, and guide enterprises to be honest and trustworthy.

Article 12 Units and individuals that have made outstanding contributions to the research and innovation of medical devices shall be given commendations and rewards in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State.

Article 13 Class I medical devices shall be subject to product filing management, and Class II and Class III medical devices shall be subject to product registration management.
Medical device registrants and filing persons shall strengthen the quality management of the entire life cycle of medical devices, and shall bear responsibility in accordance with law for the safety and effectiveness of medical devices throughout the entire process of research and development, production, operation, and use.

Article 15 For the filing of Class I medical device products, the filing person shall submit the filing materials to the department responsible for drug regulation of the people's government of the city divided into districts where it is located.
For an overseas filing person exporting Class I medical devices to the territory of China, the enterprise legal person within the territory of China designated by it shall submit the filing materials and the certificate issued by the competent authority of the country (region) where the filing person is located permitting the medical device to be marketed and sold to the drug regulatory department of the State Council. For innovative medical devices not marketed overseas, the certificate of the competent authority of the country (region) where the filing person is located permitting the medical device to be marketed and sold may be exempted from submission.
The filing is completed when the filing person submits the filing materials that comply with these Regulations to the department responsible for drug regulation. The department responsible for drug regulation shall, within 5 working days from the date of receiving the filing materials, publish the relevant filing information to the public through the online government service platform of the drug regulatory department of the State Council.
If the matters stated in the filing materials change, the filing shall be modified with the original filing department.

Article 16 To apply for registration of Class II medical device products, the registration applicant shall submit the registration application materials to the drug regulatory department of the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government where it is located. To apply for registration of Class III medical device products, the registration applicant shall submit the registration application materials to the drug regulatory department of the State Council.
For an overseas registration applicant exporting Class II or Class III medical devices to the territory of China, the enterprise legal person within the territory of China designated by it shall submit the registration application materials and the certificate issued by the competent authority of the country (region) where the registration applicant is located permitting the medical device to be marketed and sold to the drug regulatory department of the State Council. For innovative medical devices not marketed overseas, the certificate of the competent authority of the country (region) where the registration applicant is located permitting the medical device to be marketed and sold may be exempted from submission.
The drug regulatory department of the State Council shall stipulate the procedures and requirements for medical device registration review, and shall strengthen supervision and guidance over the registration review work of the drug regulatory departments of the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government.

Article 17 The drug regulatory department that accepts the registration application shall review the safety and effectiveness of the medical device and the quality management capability of the registration applicant to ensure the safety and effectiveness of the medical device.
The drug regulatory department that accepts the registration application shall, within 3 working days from the date of accepting the registration application, forward the registration application materials to the technical review institution. After completing the technical review, the technical review institution shall submit the review opinion to the drug regulatory department that accepted the registration application as the basis for approval.
Where the drug regulatory department that accepts the registration application considers it necessary to verify the quality management system during the organization of the technical review of the medical device, it shall organize and carry out the verification of the quality management system.

Article 18 The drug regulatory department that accepts the registration application shall make a decision within 20 working days from the date of receiving the review opinion. For those meeting the conditions, registration shall be granted and a medical device registration certificate shall be issued; for those not meeting the conditions, registration shall be denied and the reasons shall be provided in writing.
The drug regulatory department that accepts the registration application shall, within 5 working days from the date of granting registration of the medical device, publish the relevant registration information to the public through the online government service platform of the drug regulatory department of the State Council.

Article 19 For medical devices urgently needed for treating rare diseases, diseases that are seriously life-threatening and for which there is no effective treatment, and responding to public health incidents, the drug regulatory department that accepts the registration application may make a conditional approval decision and specify relevant matters in the medical device registration certificate.
In the event of an especially major public health emergency or other emergency that seriously threatens public health, the competent health department of the State Council and the disease prevention and control department of the State Council may, based on the needs of preventing and controlling the incident, propose the emergency use of medical devices. After being organized for demonstration and approved by the drug regulatory department of the State Council, such medical devices may be used urgently within a certain scope and time limit.

Article 21 Where substantive changes occur in the design, raw materials, production process, scope of application, method of use, etc. of a registered Class II or Class III medical device product, which may affect the safety or effectiveness of the medical device, the registrant shall apply to the original registration authority for undergoing change registration formalities; where other changes occur, the registrant shall file or report in accordance with the provisions of the medical product regulatory authority of the State Council.

Article 23 For a newly developed medical device that is not yet included in the classification catalog, the applicant may directly apply for product registration in accordance with the provisions of these Regulations on product registration of Class III medical devices, or may determine the product category in accordance with the classification rules and apply to the medical product regulatory authority of the State Council for category confirmation, and then apply for product registration or carry out product filing in accordance with the provisions of these Regulations.
Where an applicant directly applies for product registration of a Class III medical device, the medical product regulatory authority of the State Council shall determine the category based on the degree of risk and promptly include the approved medical device in the classification catalog. Where an applicant applies for category confirmation, the medical product regulatory authority of the State Council shall, within 20 working days from the date of accepting the application, determine the category of the medical device and notify the applicant.

Article 24 Clinical evaluation shall be conducted for the registration or filing of a medical device product; however, in any of the following circumstances, clinical evaluation may be exempted:
(1) The working mechanism is clear, the design is finalized, the production process is mature, the same type of medical device that has been marketed has been used clinically for many years without records of serious adverse events, and its routine use is not changed;
(2) Other circumstances where the safety and effectiveness of the medical device can be demonstrated through non-clinical evaluation.
The medical product regulatory authority of the State Council shall formulate guidelines for clinical evaluation of medical devices.

Article 25 Clinical evaluation of a medical device may, based on product characteristics, clinical risks, existing clinical data and other circumstances, be conducted by carrying out a clinical trial, or by analyzing and evaluating clinical literature and clinical data of the same type of medical device, to demonstrate the safety and effectiveness of the medical device.
Where, in accordance with the provisions of the medical product regulatory authority of the State Council, during clinical evaluation of a medical device, the existing clinical literature and clinical data are insufficient to confirm the safety and effectiveness of the product, a clinical trial shall be conducted.

Article 26 Clinical trials of medical devices shall be conducted in clinical trial institutions with appropriate conditions in accordance with the requirements of the quality management standards for medical device clinical trials, and shall be filed with the medical product regulatory authority of the people's government of the province, autonomous region or municipality directly under the Central Government where the clinical trial sponsor is located. The medical product regulatory authority that accepts the clinical trial filing shall notify the medical product regulatory authority at the same level and the health authority in the place where the clinical trial institution is located of the filing information.
Clinical trial institutions for medical devices shall be subject to filing management. The conditions to be met by medical device clinical trial institutions, as well as the filing management measures and quality management standards for clinical trials, shall be formulated and published by the medical product regulatory authority of the State Council jointly with the health authority of the State Council.
The State supports medical institutions in conducting clinical trials, incorporates the evaluation of clinical trial conditions and capabilities into the grading review of medical institutions, and encourages medical institutions to conduct clinical trials of innovative medical devices.

Article 27 Where a clinical trial of a Class III medical device poses a relatively high risk to the human body, approval of the medical product regulatory authority of the State Council shall be obtained. When examining and approving a clinical trial, the medical product regulatory authority of the State Council shall comprehensively analyze the equipment, professional personnel and other conditions of the institution intended to undertake the clinical trial of the medical device, the degree of risk of the medical device, the clinical trial implementation plan, the clinical benefit-risk analysis report, etc., and shall make a decision and notify the clinical trial sponsor within 60 working days from the date of accepting the application. If no notification is made within the time limit, it shall be deemed as consent. If the clinical trial is approved, it shall notify the medical product regulatory authority and the health authority of the people's government of the province, autonomous region or municipality directly under the Central Government where the clinical trial institution is located.
The catalog of Class III medical devices whose clinical trials pose a relatively high risk to the human body shall be formulated, adjusted and published by the medical product regulatory authority of the State Council.

Article 28 When conducting a clinical trial of a medical device, ethical review shall be conducted in accordance with the provisions, detailed information such as the purpose, use and possible risks of the trial shall be informed to the subject, and the written informed consent of the subject shall be obtained; where the subject is a person without capacity for civil conduct or a person with limited capacity for civil conduct, the written informed consent of his or her guardian shall be obtained according to law.
When conducting a clinical trial, fees related to the clinical trial shall not be charged to the subject in any form.

Article 29 For a medical device that is being used in an ongoing clinical trial for the treatment of a disease that seriously endangers life and for which there is no effective treatment, if medical observation indicates that it may benefit the patient, after ethical review and informed consent, it may be used free of charge on other patients with the same condition within the institution conducting the clinical trial of the medical device, and its safety data may be used for the medical device registration application.

Article 31 Where a person engages in the production of a Class I medical device, he or she shall file with the department responsible for medical product regulation of the people's government at the city with districts level where he or she is located, and the filing shall be completed upon submission of relevant materials meeting the conditions specified in Article 30 of these Regulations.
Where a medical device filer produces a Class I medical device on its own, it may, when carrying out product filing in accordance with Article 15 of these Regulations, simultaneously submit relevant materials meeting the conditions specified in Article 30 of these Regulations, and the production filing shall be completed.

Article 32 Where a person engages in the production of a Class II or Class III medical device, he or she shall apply to the medical product regulatory authority of the people's government of the province, autonomous region or municipality directly under the Central Government where he or she is located for a production permit and submit relevant materials showing compliance with the conditions specified in Article 30 of these Regulations as well as the registration certificate of the medical device produced.
The medical product regulatory authority that accepts the application for a production permit shall review the application materials, conduct an inspection in accordance with the requirements of the medical device production quality management standards formulated by the medical product regulatory authority of the State Council, and make a decision within 20 working days from the date of accepting the application. If the conditions prescribed are met, the permit shall be granted and a medical device production permit shall be issued; if the conditions prescribed are not met, the permit shall not be granted and reasons shall be given in writing.
The term of validity of a medical device production permit shall be five years. If renewal is required upon expiration of the term of validity, renewal formalities shall be handled in accordance with the legal provisions on administrative licenses.

Article 33 The medical device production quality management standards shall clearly stipulate matters affecting the safety and effectiveness of medical devices, such as design and development, production equipment conditions, raw material procurement, production process control, product release, and the organizational structure and staffing of the enterprise.

Article 34 A medical device registrant or filer may produce medical devices on its own, or may entrust a qualified enterprise that complies with the provisions of these Regulations and has appropriate conditions to produce medical devices.
Where the production of medical devices is entrusted, the medical device registrant or filer shall be responsible for the quality of the medical devices produced under entrustment and shall strengthen the management of the production activities of the entrusted production enterprise, ensuring that production is carried out in accordance with the statutory requirements. The medical device registrant or filer shall sign an entrustment agreement with the entrusted production enterprise, specifying the rights, obligations and responsibilities of both parties. The entrusted production enterprise shall organize production in accordance with laws and regulations, the medical device production quality management standards, mandatory standards, product technical requirements and the entrustment agreement, be responsible for production activities, and accept supervision by the entrusting party.
Implantable medical devices with high risks shall not be produced under entrustment. The specific catalog shall be formulated, adjusted and published by the medical product regulatory authority of the State Council.

Article 35 A medical device registrant, filer or entrusted production enterprise shall, in accordance with the medical device production quality management standards, establish and improve a quality management system suitable for the medical devices produced and ensure its effective operation; organize production strictly in accordance with the product technical requirements approved or filed, and ensure that the medical devices leaving the factory comply with mandatory standards and the product technical requirements approved or filed.
A medical device registrant, filer or entrusted production enterprise shall periodically conduct self-inspection on the operation of the quality management system and submit a self-inspection report in accordance with the provisions of the medical product regulatory authority of the State Council.

Article 36 Where the production conditions of a medical device change and no longer meet the requirements of the medical device quality management system, the medical device registrant, filer or entrusted production enterprise shall immediately take corrective measures; where it may affect the safety or effectiveness of the medical device, production activities shall be immediately suspended and the original production permit or production filing authority shall be reported to.
Article 37 A medical device shall use a common name. The common name shall comply with the medical device naming rules formulated by the medical product regulatory authority of the State Council.

Article 38 The State shall, based on the categories of medical device products, implement the unique device identification system step by step to achieve traceability of medical devices. The specific measures shall be formulated by the medical product regulatory authority of the State Council jointly with the relevant departments of the State Council.

Article 40 A person engaged in the operation of medical devices shall have business premises and storage conditions commensurate with the scale and scope of the business, and have a quality management system and a quality management institution or personnel suitable for the medical devices operated.

Article 41 Anyone engaging in the operation of Class II medical devices shall file with the department responsible for drug administration under the people's government at the districted city level in its locality and submit relevant materials that meet the conditions prescribed in Article 40 of these Regulations.
In accordance with the provisions of the drug administration department under the State Council, for Class II medical devices whose safety and effectiveness are not affected by the circulation process, the filing for operation may be exempted.

Article 42 Anyone engaging in the operation of Class III medical devices shall apply for an operation license to the department responsible for drug administration under the people's government at the districted city level in its locality and submit relevant materials that meet the conditions prescribed in Article 40 of these Regulations.
The department responsible for drug administration that accepts the application for an operation license shall review the application materials, organize verification where necessary, and make a decision within 20 working days from the date of accepting the application. Where the conditions prescribed are met, the license shall be granted and a medical device operation license shall be issued; where the conditions are not met, the license shall not be granted and reasons shall be given in writing.
The validity period of a medical device operation license is five years. Where the license needs to be renewed after expiry, the renewal formalities shall be handled in accordance with the legal provisions on administrative licensing.

Article 43 A medical device registrant or filing person that operates the medical devices it has registered or filed does not need to apply for a medical device operation license or file, but shall meet the operation conditions prescribed in these Regulations.

Article 44 Anyone engaged in the operation of medical devices shall, in accordance with laws, regulations and the requirements of the medical device operation quality management standards formulated by the drug administration department under the State Council, establish and improve a quality management system commensurate with the medical devices it operates and ensure its effective operation.

Article 46 Anyone engaging in the online sale of medical devices shall be a medical device registrant, filing person or medical device operation enterprise. An operator engaging in the online sale of medical devices shall notify the department responsible for drug administration under the people's government at the districted city level in its locality of the relevant information about its online sale, except for those operating Class I medical devices and the Class II medical devices specified in the second paragraph of Article 41 of these Regulations.
An e-commerce platform operator providing services for medical device online transactions shall conduct real-name registration of medical device operators on the platform, review their operation licenses or filings and the registration or filing status of the medical device products they operate, and manage their operation activities. Where the e-commerce platform operator discovers that a medical device operator on the platform has violated the provisions of these Regulations, it shall promptly stop such conduct and immediately report to the department responsible for drug administration under the people's government at the districted city level in the locality of the medical device operator; where a serious violation is discovered, it shall immediately stop providing online trading platform services.

Article 47 The transport and storage of medical devices shall comply with the requirements indicated in the instructions and labels of the medical devices; where there are special requirements for environmental conditions such as temperature and humidity, corresponding measures shall be taken to ensure the safety and effectiveness of the medical devices.

Article 48 A medical device using unit shall have storage premises and conditions commensurate with the variety and quantity of medical devices in use. The medical device using unit shall strengthen technical training for its staff and use medical devices in accordance with the requirements of product instructions and technical operation specifications.
Where a medical device using unit configures large-scale medical equipment, it shall comply with the large-scale medical equipment allocation plan formulated by the health主管部门 under the State Council, be commensurate with its functional positioning and clinical service needs, have corresponding technical conditions, supporting facilities, and professional technical personnel with corresponding qualifications and capabilities, and obtain approval from the health主管部门 under the people's government at or above the provincial level, and obtain a large-scale medical equipment allocation license.
The measures for the administration of large-scale medical equipment allocation shall be formulated by the health主管部门 under the State Council jointly with the relevant departments under the State Council. The catalogue of large-scale medical equipment shall be proposed by the health主管部门 under the State Council in consultation with the relevant departments under the State Council and implemented after being submitted to the State Council for approval.

Article 49 A medical device using unit shall handle reusable medical devices in accordance with the provisions on disinfection and management formulated by the health主管部门 under the State Council.
Single-use medical devices shall not be reused; used single-use medical devices shall be destroyed and recorded in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State. The catalogue of single-use medical devices shall be formulated, adjusted and published by the drug administration department under the State Council jointly with the health主管部门 under the State Council. The inclusion of a medical device in the catalogue of single-use medical devices shall be based on sufficient evidence and reasons that it cannot be reused. Medical devices that can be reused while ensuring safety and effectiveness shall not be included in the catalogue of single-use medical devices. Where, due to improvements in design, production process, disinfection and sterilization technology, etc., a medical device can be reused while ensuring safety and effectiveness, it shall be removed from the catalogue of single-use medical devices and allowed to be reused.

Article 50 For medical devices that require regular inspection, testing, calibration, maintenance and servicing, a medical device using unit shall perform such actions in accordance with the product instructions, keep records, and promptly conduct analysis and evaluation to ensure that the medical devices are in good condition and guarantee their use quality; for large-scale medical devices with a long service life, use files shall be established for each device, recording its use, maintenance, transfer, actual use time, etc. The records shall be kept for no less than five years after the expiry of the prescribed service life of the medical device.

Article 51 A medical device using unit shall properly keep the original materials of purchased Class III medical devices and ensure the traceability of the information.
Where large-scale medical devices or implantable and interventional medical devices are used, the name, key technical parameters and other information of the medical device, as well as necessary information closely related to the safety of use quality, shall be recorded in the medical records and other relevant records.

Article 52 Where a medical device in use is found to have safety hazards, the medical device using unit shall immediately stop using it and notify the medical device registrant, filing person or other institution responsible for product quality to carry out repair and inspection; if the medical device still fails to meet the safety standards for use after repair and inspection, it shall not be used further.

Article 53 For in vitro diagnostic reagents for which no product of the same kind has been marketed in China, a medical institution that meets the conditions may, based on its own clinical needs, self-develop such reagents and use them within the institution under the guidance of a licensed physician. The specific measures for administration shall be formulated by the drug administration department under the State Council jointly with the health主管部门 under the State Council.

Article 54 The department responsible for drug administration and the health主管部门 shall, in accordance with their respective functions and duties, supervise and administer the quality of medical devices in the use process and the conduct of medical device use respectively.

Article 55 No medical device operation enterprise or using unit may operate or use medical devices that are not registered or filed in accordance with law, have no certificate of conformity, or are expired, invalid, or eliminated.

Article 56 Where medical devices in use are transferred between medical device using units, the transferor shall ensure that the transferred medical devices are safe and effective, and may not transfer expired, invalid, eliminated medical devices or those that have failed inspection.

Article 57 Imported medical devices shall be those that have been registered or filed in accordance with the provisions of Chapter II of these Regulations.
Imported medical devices shall have Chinese instructions and Chinese labels. The instructions and labels shall comply with the provisions of these Regulations and the requirements of relevant mandatory standards, and the instructions shall indicate the place of origin of the medical device and the name, address and contact information of the domestic enterprise legal person designated by the overseas medical device registrant or filing person. Importation shall not be permitted if there are no Chinese instructions or Chinese labels, or if the instructions or labels do not comply with the provisions of this Article.
Where a medical institution urgently needs to import a small quantity of Class II or Class III medical devices for clinical needs, importation may be permitted upon approval by the drug administration department under the State Council or the people's government of a province, autonomous region or municipality directly under the State Council authorized by the State Council. The imported medical devices shall be used for specific medical purposes within the designated medical institution.
The importation of used medical devices such as those that are expired, invalid or eliminated is prohibited.

Article 58 The exit-entry inspection and quarantine authorities shall, in accordance with law, carry out inspection on imported medical devices; those failing the inspection shall not be imported.
The drug administration department under the State Council shall promptly notify the national exit-entry inspection and quarantine department of the registration and filing status of imported medical devices. The exit-entry inspection and quarantine authority at the place of the import port shall promptly notify the department responsible for drug administration under the people's government at the districted city level in its locality of the customs clearance status of imported medical devices.
Article 59 An enterprise that exports medical devices shall ensure that the exported medical devices meet the requirements of the importing country (region).

Article 60 The content of medical device advertisements shall be truthful and lawful, based on the instructions of the medical device registered or filed with the department responsible for drug administration, and shall not contain false, exaggerated or misleading content.
Before publishing a medical device advertisement, the content of the advertisement shall be reviewed by the advertisement review authority designated by the people's government of a province, autonomous region or municipality directly under the State Council, and an approval number for the medical device advertisement shall be obtained; without review, the advertisement shall not be published.
For medical devices whose production, import, operation and use have been ordered to be suspended by the drug administration department under the people's government at or above the provincial level, advertisements involving such medical devices shall not be published during the suspension period.
The measures for review of medical device advertisements shall be formulated by the market regulation department under the State Council.
Article 61 The State shall establish a monitoring system for adverse events of medical devices to collect, analyze, evaluate, and control adverse events of medical devices in a timely manner.

Article 62 A medical device registrant or record-filing entity shall establish a monitoring system for adverse events of medical devices, equip with adverse event monitoring institutions and personnel commensurate with its products, proactively carry out adverse event monitoring for its products, and report investigations, analyses, evaluations, product risk controls, and other information to the technical institution for adverse event monitoring of medical devices in accordance with the provisions of the drug regulatory department of the State Council.
A medical device production or operating enterprise or a using entity shall assist the medical device registrant or record-filing entity in carrying out adverse event monitoring for the medical devices it produces, operates, or uses; upon discovering an adverse event or suspected adverse event of a medical device, it shall report to the technical institution for adverse event monitoring of medical devices in accordance with the provisions of the drug regulatory department of the State Council.
Other entities or individuals discovering an adverse event or suspected adverse event of a medical device shall have the right to report to the drug regulatory department or the technical institution for adverse event monitoring of medical devices.

Article 63 The drug regulatory department of the State Council shall strengthen the construction of an information network for adverse event monitoring of medical devices.
A technical institution for adverse event monitoring of medical devices shall strengthen the monitoring of adverse event information of medical devices and proactively collect adverse event information; upon discovering an adverse event or receiving a report of an adverse event, it shall promptly verify, and if necessary, investigate, analyze, and evaluate, and report to the drug regulatory department and the competent health department, and propose handling suggestions.
A technical institution for adverse event monitoring of medical devices shall make public its contact information to facilitate reporting of adverse events of medical devices by medical device registrants, record-filing entities, production and operating enterprises, using entities, and others.

Article 64 The drug regulatory department shall, based on the evaluation results of adverse events of medical devices, promptly take control measures such as issuing warning information and ordering the suspension of production, import, operation, and use.
The drug regulatory department of the people's government at or above the provincial level shall, jointly with the competent health department at the same level and relevant departments, organize timely investigation and handling of adverse events of medical devices that cause sudden, group-occurring serious injury or death, and organize strengthened monitoring of similar medical devices.
The drug regulatory department shall promptly notify the competent health department at the same level of the relevant situation of adverse event monitoring of medical device using entities.

Article 65 A medical device registrant, record-filing entity, production or operating enterprise, or using entity shall cooperate with the investigations of adverse events of medical devices conducted by the technical institution for adverse event monitoring of medical devices, the drug regulatory department, and the competent health department.

Article 66 Under any of the following circumstances, a medical device registrant or record-filing entity shall proactively carry out re-evaluation of marketed medical devices:
(1) there is a change in understanding of the safety or effectiveness of a medical device based on the development of scientific research;
(2) the monitoring or evaluation results of adverse events of medical devices indicate that a medical device may have defects;
(3) other circumstances specified by the drug regulatory department of the State Council.
A medical device registrant or record-filing entity shall, based on the re-evaluation results, take corresponding control measures, make improvements to the marketed medical device, and carry out registration changes or record-filing changes in accordance with the provisions. If the re-evaluation results show that a marketed medical device cannot ensure safety and effectiveness, the medical device registrant or record-filing entity shall proactively apply for cancellation of the medical device registration certificate or withdrawal of the record-filing; if the medical device registrant or record-filing entity fails to apply for cancellation of the medical device registration certificate or withdrawal of the record-filing, the drug regulatory department shall cancel the medical device registration certificate or withdraw the record-filing.
The drug regulatory department of the people's government at or above the provincial level shall conduct re-evaluation of marketed medical devices based on adverse event monitoring, evaluation, and other circumstances. If the re-evaluation results show that a marketed medical device cannot ensure safety and effectiveness, the medical device registration certificate shall be cancelled or the record-filing shall be withdrawn.
The drug regulatory department shall promptly make public the cancellation of medical device registration certificates and withdrawal of record-filings. A medical device whose registration certificate has been cancelled or whose record-filing has been withdrawn shall not continue to be produced, imported, operated, or used.

Article 67 If a medical device registrant or record-filing entity discovers that a medical device it produces does not comply with mandatory standards, the product technical requirements approved upon registration or recorded, or has other defects, it shall immediately stop production, notify relevant operating enterprises, using entities, and consumers to stop operation and use, recall the medical devices already placed on the market, take remedial, destruction, and other measures, record relevant information, release relevant information, and report the recall and handling of the medical device to the drug regulatory department and the competent health department.
If a medical device entrusted production enterprise or operating enterprise discovers that the medical device it produces or operates falls under the circumstances set forth in the preceding paragraph, it shall immediately stop production or operation, notify the medical device registrant or record-filing entity, and record the stoppage of production or operation and the notification. If the medical device registrant or record-filing entity considers that the medical device needs to be recalled in accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph, it shall recall it immediately.
If a medical device registrant, record-filing entity, entrusted production enterprise, or operating enterprise fails to implement a recall or stop production or operation in accordance with this Article, the drug regulatory department may order it to recall or stop production or operation.
Article 68 The State shall establish a system of professional and specialized inspectors to strengthen the supervision and inspection of medical devices.

Article 71 The competent health department shall strengthen supervision and inspection of the use of medical devices by medical institutions. When conducting supervision and inspection, it may enter medical institutions and review and copy relevant archives, records, and other relevant materials.

Article 72 Where there are potential product quality and safety hazards during the production or operation of medical devices, and measures are not taken in a timely manner to eliminate them, the drug regulatory department may take measures such as issuing warnings, conducting responsibility interviews, and ordering rectification within a time limit.
For medical devices that cause harm to the human body or for which there is evidence proving they may endanger human health, the drug regulatory department may take emergency control measures such as ordering the suspension of production, import, operation, and use, and issue safety warning information.

Article 73 The drug regulatory department shall strengthen random inspection and testing of medical devices produced, operated, or used by medical device registrants, record-filing entities, production and operating enterprises, and using entities. Random inspection and testing shall not charge inspection fees or any other fees, and the necessary expenses shall be included in the government budget at the corresponding level. The drug regulatory department of the people's government at or above the provincial level shall, based on the results of random inspection and testing, promptly publish medical device quality bulletins.
The competent health department shall supervise and evaluate the use of large medical equipment; upon discovering irregular use and situations such as excessive examination or excessive treatment related to large medical equipment, it shall immediately correct and handle according to law.

Article 74 Where a drug regulatory department fails to timely discover systemic risks in medical device safety or fails to timely eliminate potential medical device safety hazards within its supervisory and administrative area, the people's government at the same level or the drug regulatory department of the people's government at a higher level shall conduct an interview with its principal responsible person.
Where a local people's government fails to perform its duties concerning medical device safety or fails to timely eliminate major regional medical device safety hazards, the people's government at a higher level or the drug regulatory department of the people's government at a higher level shall conduct an interview with its principal responsible person.
The interviewed department and local people's government shall immediately take measures to rectify the medical device supervision and administration work.

Article 75 The qualification accreditation of medical device testing institutions shall be uniformly managed in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State. Only a testing institution accredited by the certification and accreditation regulatory department of the State Council jointly with the drug regulatory department of the State Council may conduct testing on medical devices.
Where a drug regulatory department needs to test a medical device in its law enforcement work, it shall entrust a qualified medical device testing institution to do so and pay the relevant fees.
If a party disagrees with the test conclusion, it may, within 7 working days from the date of receipt of the test conclusion, apply for a re-test to the department that conducted the sampling test or the drug regulatory department at the next higher level. The department accepting the re-test application shall randomly determine a re-test institution from the list of re-test institutions to conduct the re-test. The medical device testing institution undertaking the re-test shall issue a re-test conclusion within the time limit prescribed by the drug regulatory department of the State Council. The re-test conclusion shall be the final test conclusion. The re-test institution and the initial test institution shall not be the same institution; if only one qualified testing institution exists for the relevant test item, the undertaking department or personnel shall be changed for the re-test. The list of re-test institutions shall be published by the drug regulatory department of the State Council.

Article 76 For medical devices that may contain harmful substances or have unauthorized changes in design, raw materials, or production processes and have potential safety hazards, and for which testing cannot be conducted in accordance with the test items and test methods specified in the national standards or industry standards for medical devices, a medical device testing institution may use supplementary test items and test methods approved by the drug regulatory department of the State Council for testing; the test conclusions obtained using supplementary test items and test methods may serve as the basis for the drug regulatory department to determine the quality of the medical device.

Article 77 The market regulatory department shall, in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and administrative regulations on advertising management, supervise and inspect medical device advertisements and investigate and deal with illegal acts.

Article 78 The drug regulatory department shall, through the online government service platform of the drug regulatory department of the State Council, timely publish daily supervision and administration information on medical device licensing, record-filing, random inspection and testing, investigation and punishment of illegal acts, and other matters in accordance with law. However, the trade secrets of the parties shall not be disclosed.
The drug regulatory department shall establish credit files for medical device registrants, record-filing entities, production and operating enterprises, and using entities, increase the frequency of supervision and inspection for those with adverse credit records, and strengthen punishment for dishonesty in accordance with law.

Article 79 The drug regulatory department and other relevant departments shall make public their contact information and accept inquiries, complaints, and reports. Upon receiving an inquiry related to medical device supervision and administration, the drug regulatory department or other relevant departments shall promptly reply; upon receiving a complaint or report, they shall promptly verify, handle, and reply. The inquiries, complaints, reports, and the corresponding replies, verifications, and handling situations shall be recorded and kept.
If a report concerning the research and development, production, operation, or use of a medical device is verified to be true after investigation, the drug regulatory department or other relevant departments shall reward the person who made the report. The relevant departments shall keep the confidentiality of the person who made the report.

Article 80 When the drug regulatory department of the State Council formulates, adjusts, or revises the catalogs specified in these Regulations and the norms related to medical device supervision and administration, it shall solicit public comments; and by means such as holding hearings, feasibility discussion meetings, etc., it shall hear the opinions of experts, medical device registrants, record-filing entities, production and operating enterprises, using entities, consumers, industry associations, and relevant organizations.

Article 82 Where a large-scale medical device is deployed and used without a license, the health authority of the people's government at or above the county level shall order cessation of use, give a warning, and confiscate the illegal gains; if the illegal gains are less than RMB 10,000 Yuan, a fine of not less than RMB 50,000 Yuan but not more than RMB 100,000 Yuan shall also be imposed; if the illegal gains are RMB 10,000 Yuan or more, a fine of not less than 10 times but not more than 30 times the illegal gains shall also be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, no application for a large-scale medical device deployment permit submitted by the relevant responsible persons and the entity shall be accepted within 5 years, and the legal representative, principal responsible person, directly responsible supervisor and other responsible persons of the illegal entity shall have their income obtained from the entity during the period when the illegal act occurred confiscated, a fine of not less than 30% but not more than 3 times the income obtained shall also be imposed, and sanctions shall be imposed according to law.

Article 83 Where an applicant provides false materials or uses other deceptive means when applying for an administrative license for medical devices, the administrative license shall not be granted; if the administrative license has already been granted, the department that made the decision to grant the license shall revoke the administrative license, confiscate the illegal gains and the medical devices illegally produced, operated or used, and no application for a medical device license submitted by the relevant responsible persons and the entity shall be accepted within 10 years; if the value of the illegally produced, operated or used medical devices is less than RMB 10,000 Yuan, a fine of not less than RMB 50,000 Yuan but not more than RMB 150,000 Yuan shall also be imposed; if the value is RMB 10,000 Yuan or more, a fine of not less than 15 times but not more than 30 times the value of the goods shall also be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, the production or business operation shall be ordered to suspend for rectification, and the legal representative, principal responsible person, directly responsible supervisor and other responsible persons of the illegal entity shall have their income obtained from the entity during the period when the illegal act occurred confiscated, a fine of not less than 30% but not more than 3 times the income obtained shall also be imposed, and they shall be permanently prohibited from engaging in the production or operation of medical devices.
Where a person forges, alters, buys, sells, leases, or lends a relevant medical device license, the original issuing authority shall confiscate or revoke the license, and confiscate the illegal gains; if the illegal gains are less than RMB 10,000 Yuan, a fine of not less than RMB 50,000 Yuan but not more than RMB 100,000 Yuan shall also be imposed; if the illegal gains are RMB 10,000 Yuan or more, a fine of not less than 10 times but not more than 20 times the illegal gains shall also be imposed; if the act constitutes a violation of public security administration, the public security organ shall impose a public security administration penalty according to law.

Article 85 Where a person provides false materials when filing, the drug regulatory authority shall announce the name of the filing entity and the product to the public, confiscate the illegal gains and the medical devices illegally produced or operated; if the value of the illegally produced or operated medical devices is less than RMB 10,000 Yuan, a fine of not less than RMB 20,000 Yuan but not more than RMB 50,000 Yuan shall also be imposed; if the value is RMB 10,000 Yuan or more, a fine of not less than 5 times but not more than 20 times the value of the goods shall also be imposed; if the circumstances are serious, the production or business operation shall be ordered to suspend for rectification, and the legal representative, principal responsible person, directly responsible supervisor and other responsible persons of the illegal entity shall have their income obtained from the entity during the period when the illegal act occurred confiscated, a fine of not less than 30% but not more than 3 times the income obtained shall also be imposed, and they shall be prohibited from engaging in the production or operation of medical devices for 10 years.

Article 87 Where a medical device business enterprise or user fulfills the obligations of incoming inspection and other obligations as prescribed in these Regulations, has sufficient evidence to prove that it did not know that the medical devices it operated or used were those specified in Article 81, paragraph 1, item (1), Article 84, item (1), Article 86, items (1) and (3) of these Regulations, and can truthfully explain the source of purchase, the medical devices it operates or uses that do not meet the statutory requirements shall be confiscated, and the administrative penalty may be exempted.

Article 91 Where a medical device is imported in violation of the laws and administrative regulations on the inspection of import and export commodities, the entry-exit inspection and quarantine authority shall handle the matter according to law.

Article 92 Where an e-commerce platform operator providing services for online trading of medical devices violates these Regulations by failing to fulfill the management obligations of registering the real names of medical device operators on the platform, reviewing their licenses, registrations and filings, stopping and reporting illegal acts, or ceasing to provide online trading platform services, the drug regulatory authority shall impose a penalty in accordance with the provisions of the E-Commerce Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 93 Where a clinical trial is conducted without filing the clinical trial institution for medical devices, the drug regulatory authority shall order cessation of the clinical trial and rectification; if no rectification is made, the clinical trial data shall not be used for product registration or filing, a fine of not less than RMB 50,000 Yuan but not more than RMB 100,000 Yuan shall be imposed, and a public announcement shall be made; if serious consequences are caused, the entity shall be prohibited from conducting clinical trials on relevant medical devices for 5 years, a fine of not less than RMB 100,000 Yuan but not more than RMB 300,000 Yuan shall also be imposed, and the health authority shall confiscate the income obtained from the entity during the period when the illegal act occurred from the legal representative, principal responsible person, directly responsible supervisor and other responsible persons of the illegal entity, impose a fine of not less than 30% but not more than 3 times the income obtained, and impose sanctions according to law.
Where a clinical trial sponsor conducts a clinical trial without filing, the drug regulatory authority shall order cessation of the clinical trial, impose a fine of not less than RMB 50,000 Yuan but not more than RMB 100,000 Yuan on the clinical trial sponsor, and make a public announcement; if serious consequences are caused, a fine of not less than RMB 100,000 Yuan but not more than RMB 300,000 Yuan shall be imposed. The clinical trial data shall not be used for product registration or filing, and no application for medical device registration submitted by the relevant responsible persons and the entity shall be accepted within 5 years.
Where a clinical trial sponsor conducts a clinical trial for a Class III medical device that poses a relatively high risk to the human body without approval, the drug regulatory authority shall order immediate cessation of the clinical trial, impose a fine of not less than RMB 100,000 Yuan but not more than RMB 300,000 Yuan on the clinical trial sponsor, and make a public announcement; if serious consequences are caused, a fine of not less than RMB 300,000 Yuan but not more than RMB 1,000,000 Yuan shall be imposed. The clinical trial data shall not be used for product registration, and no application for clinical trial or registration of medical devices submitted by the relevant responsible persons and the entity shall be accepted within 10 years; the legal representative, principal responsible person, directly responsible supervisor and other responsible persons of the illegal entity shall have their income obtained from the entity during the period when the illegal act occurred confiscated, and a fine of not less than 30% but not more than 3 times the income obtained shall also be imposed.

Article 94 Where a medical device clinical trial institution conducts a medical device clinical trial without complying with the clinical trial quality management standards, the drug regulatory authority shall order rectification or immediate cessation of the clinical trial, and impose a fine of not less than RMB 50,000 Yuan but not more than RMB 100,000 Yuan; if serious consequences are caused, the institution shall be prohibited from conducting clinical trials on relevant medical devices for 5 years, and the health authority shall confiscate the income obtained from the entity during the period when the illegal act occurred from the legal representative, principal responsible person, directly responsible supervisor and other responsible persons of the illegal entity, impose a fine of not less than 30% but not more than 3 times the income obtained, and impose sanctions according to law.

Article 95 Where a medical device clinical trial institution issues a false report, the drug regulatory authority shall impose a fine of not less than RMB 100,000 Yuan but not more than RMB 300,000 Yuan; if there are illegal gains, the illegal gains shall be confiscated; the institution shall be prohibited from conducting clinical trials on relevant medical devices for 10 years; and the health authority shall confiscate the income obtained from the entity during the period when the illegal act occurred from the legal representative, principal responsible person, directly responsible supervisor and other responsible persons of the illegal entity, impose a fine of not less than 30% but not more than 3 times the income obtained, and impose sanctions according to law.

Article 96 Where a medical device testing institution issues a false testing report, the competent authority that granted its qualification shall revoke the testing qualification, no application for qualification accreditation submitted by the relevant responsible persons and the entity shall be accepted within 10 years, and a fine of not less than RMB 100,000 Yuan but not more than RMB 300,000 Yuan shall be imposed; if there are illegal gains, the illegal gains shall be confiscated; for the legal representative, principal responsible person, directly responsible supervisor and other responsible persons of the illegal entity, the income obtained from the entity during the period when the illegal act occurred shall be confiscated, a fine of not less than 30% but not more than 3 times the income obtained shall also be imposed, and sanctions shall be imposed according to law; if a person is dismissed, he or she shall be prohibited from engaging in medical device testing work for 10 years.

Article 97 Where the provisions of these Regulations on the administration of medical device advertisements are violated, a penalty shall be imposed in accordance with the provisions of the Advertising Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 98 Where a domestic enterprise legal person designated by an overseas medical device registrant or filer fails to perform the relevant obligations in accordance with these Regulations, the drug regulatory authority of the people's government of a province, autonomous region or municipality directly under the Central Government shall order rectification, give a warning, and impose a fine of not less than RMB 50,000 Yuan but not more than RMB 100,000 Yuan; if the circumstances are serious, a fine of not less than RMB 100,000 Yuan but not more than RMB 500,000 Yuan shall be imposed, and its legal representative, principal responsible person, directly responsible supervisor and other responsible persons shall be prohibited from engaging in the production or operation of medical devices for 5 years.
Where an overseas medical device registrant or filer refuses to comply with the administrative penalty decision made in accordance with these Regulations, the import of its medical devices shall be prohibited for 10 years.

Article 99 Where a medical device research, production or operation entity or testing institution employs a person who is prohibited from engaging in the production, operation or testing of medical devices in violation of these Regulations, the drug regulatory authority shall order rectification and give a warning; if no rectification is made, the entity shall be ordered to suspend production or business operation until its license is revoked.

Article 100 Where a medical device technical review institution or a medical device adverse event monitoring technical institution fails to perform its duties in accordance with these Regulations, causing major errors in the review or monitoring work, the drug regulatory authority shall order rectification, circulate a notice of criticism, and give a warning; if serious consequences are caused, sanctions shall be imposed on the legal representative, principal responsible person, directly responsible supervisor and other responsible persons of the illegal entity according to law.

Article 101 Where staff members of the drug regulatory department or other relevant departments violate the provisions of these Regulations by abusing their powers, neglecting their duties, or engaging in malpractices for personal gain, they shall be given a sanction according to law.

Article 102 Any violation of the provisions of these Regulations that constitutes a crime shall be subject to criminal liability according to law; and any damage to person, property, or other damages caused shall be subject to compensation liability according to law.

Article 104 Fees may be charged for medical device product registration. The specific fee items and standards shall be formulated by the finance department and the price department of the State Council respectively in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State.

Article 105 The administrative measures for medical devices developed by medical and health institutions for responding to public health emergencies shall be formulated by the drug regulatory department of the State Council jointly with the health department of the State Council.
The storage, allocation, and supply of non-profit contraceptive medical devices shall comply with the administrative measures formulated by the health department of the State Council jointly with the drug regulatory department of the State Council.
The technical guidance principles for traditional Chinese medicine medical devices shall be formulated by the drug regulatory department of the State Council jointly with the traditional Chinese medicine department of the State Council.
Article 106 The supervision and administration of the use of medical devices in the military shall be executed in accordance with these Regulations and the relevant provisions of the military.
Article 107 These Regulations shall come into force as of June 1, 2021.
